_about: AI weights (SPEC §12.3, §17), map-level only (in-battle tactic and retreat weights come later). A field squad, when idle, scores holding the building it's on against moving to each neutral or player-held town, tower or temple (worth least, session 059) no other enemy squad is after (EnemyAI).
_refuge_types: User, 2026-11-13: an enemy squad that has lost go_home_fallen_share of its units (or its leader) falls back to the nearest building of these types the enemy holds with no hostile squad on it (the Enemy Base if none), and brings its fallen back there. Its fallen also come back while it stands still on any of them.

field._value: A building's worth: type_value × (1 + middle_weight × how central it is between the two bases, 0 at a base to 1 midway) × player_held if the player holds it.
field._hold: Holding: the value × (hold_base + threat_weight × min(1, player Threat within threat_radius ÷ the squad's own Threat)); 0 if another enemy squad already holds it.
field._move: Moving: the target's value ÷ (1 + distance ÷ distance_range), distance_range given for a 400-wide map, scaled up for wider maps (never down).
field._choice: The higher score wins logic_chance of the time; otherwise a coin flip between holding and the best move. A holding squad thinks again after rethink_ticks.

force._forward: Playtest round 19 (user, 2026-11-15: on small boards the enemy came too late): besides the usual squads, this many more front squads start in each of the two quadrants of your half of the map (either side of the line between the bases), each on a neutral town or tower there, the one at the middle distance from your base, so battles begin sooner. Not in Quick start.
force._note: Playtest round 16 (pace and board scale, lever 2; user 2026-11-15: not one lane): of the enemy's field squads, raider_share are raiders (free to go anywhere, keen on your buildings), occupier_share hold the towns and towers nearest the Enemy Base, and the rest are the front. front_starts of the front start in towns of their own across the enemy's half of the map, picked far apart, so the front opens on several lanes; the rest start at the base. Quick start keeps its own setup (the Garrison and the Raiders).

front._note: A front squad only goes for buildings within reach hexes (given for a 400-wide map, scaled up for wider ones, never down) of ground the enemy holds: a building of its or the Enemy Base, so it pushes out from its territory instead of leapfrogging. A raider's targets have no such limit, and a building you hold is worth raider_player_weight times more to it (on top of field.player_held).

hunt._note: Playtest round 16 (user 2026-11-15: the enemy wants your squads out of its backfield). When a front squad first sees one of your squads (within sight hexes), it turns to chase it with a chance of per_building for each building the enemy holds (towns, towers and the Enemy Base) that your squad is nearer to than it is: 1 building 25%, 2 50%, 3 75%, 4 or more always. It follows your squad until it fights it or loses sight of it, then goes back to its own plans; the roll comes again once your squad has left its sight (or after a fight). Raiders and holdfasts never chase.

dodge._crawl_detour: Playtest round 21 (user 2026-11-15): a leaderless squad (either side) heads only for its own base and can't take buildings; it routes round the other side's squads standing still (yours only those it can see) if that route is at most crawl_detour times the straight one, else it goes straight.
dodge._note: Playtest rounds 15 and 16 (user 2026-11-15): an enemy squad falling back to recover routes round your squads that are standing still (not ones on the move: you have to move to catch it). A raider routes round all your squads, keeping a hex clear of each, raider_chance of the times it sets off for a new target: sneaking behind your lines. Where there's no way round, it goes straight.

battle._note: How enemy squads fight (SPEC 12.3: the AI's target priority and retreat threshold in data; built 2026-11-15). Each enemy squad rolls its battle tactic once, by tactic_weights, and keeps it (the battle's middle box names it). From the second round, once it has lost at least retreat_after_loss of the HP it began the battle with, and at least losing_ratio times the share your side has lost (clearly losing; battles last about three rounds), it tries to retreat at the start of each round, with the same chance yours has (battle.json retreat; a failure costs its next action). Squads in holders (the Warlord, the base guard, holdfasts) never retreat: they hold their ground.

volleys._note: Enemy ranged attacks on the map (SPEC 11.2 for both sides; built 2026-11-15): an enemy squad with Ranged or Magic units in position fires on one of your squads in range (rules.json ranged_attack: 2 hexes, 3 from high ground), the nearest, whenever its cooldown is over and no other fight has started that tick. Not while falling back to recover. Off: only you fire from a distance.
